jobs.description: Silver load of 차세대 온비드 public sale (root ADR-0280; the publisher's load-data-go-kr-onbid-silver, DuckDB inside the publisher and its own Iceberg append, root ADR-0559): the Bronze objects no commit of their table records (plan-silver-load-objects, R2 alone), oldest first, each in its own commit, append to silver.onbid_real_estate_item the item conditions whose content changed and, when the pass was complete, a removal marker for each condition that left the list (root ADR-0275), each placed on a served parcel by the place-identity stage (the code first, then the item name's address, root ADR-0288 §1, ADR-0482), and to silver.onbid_item_bid_result each result answer; and (root ADR-0340) to the announcement, announcement bid-result, announcement detail, item detail and item bid-info tables the keys whose content changed, every column mapped from data-go-kr-onbid.fields.json. Hourly, after the collector (minute 7, at most 40 minutes); `unchanged` without starting the load when nothing is owed; no Spark.
jobs.memory_measured: journal `memory peak` 2026-10-18..11-08, 433 runs, highest 2026-10-29 (foundation-onbid-silver-load), when the load ran in the spark-small container (2560m, its own cap). Since root ADR-0559 the load is the publisher's DuckDB inside this unit: the stage's buffer is half the execution profile (2048 MiB, lakehouse-engine.contract.json), and the engine-equality harness on ai-server peaked at 1795 MiB anonymous over three production item list objects (62,235 conditions each, R2 reads and the place-identity inputs included); 3G holds the buffer and the process, and is under the 2560m container plus 1G unit it replaces
jobs.disk_measured: not measured: computed bound for a job whose command opens a DuckDB stage over tables of thousands to millions of rows (its stage database and staged files). The stage logs `duckdb stage closed: disk_bytes=<n>` as it closes (root ADR-0622); a pull request replaces this bound with the highest logged value, nothing is kept between runs.

open_exception.why: Five runs reached the 40-minute limit, 2026-10-29T22:29Z to 2026-10-30T01:50Z, catching up after #943 and #945 widened the Silver rows; since then the longest run is 1,418 s. max_objects 24 is a count with no measured object time and no deadline, so the next backlog of large objects can outlive the unit again.
open_exception.tracked_by: root ADR-0386 §5: give silver_load a run_time_budget_seconds and measured_object_seconds, as rt-molit's (#988)

expected_outcome.basis: its collector changes every hour; measured 2026-11-11 from each unit's journal, 10-12..11-11 (read-only): changed 198 of 341 runs, longest gap 93.8 h, which this bound reports.
